already-have.reason: SE-08 is not implemented anywhere in the tree, but its two main halves are already tracked as open issues. No Rust source references 0xE122, 0xE123, 0xE0C5 or a read_sec helper (rg over secure/ shared/ proto/ nonsecure/ hits only two comments: secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:1281 and secure/src/optiga_under_test/pure_tests.rs:1000). Part (a), the never-reset lifetime counter, is #485 (OPEN, TZP-14, 'ADOPT'). Part (b), the SEC read, is #275 (OPEN, se-3, advisory only). The proposal does not contradict a recorded decision; it must be reconciled with the se-3 advisory-only scoping and the S-1/S-3 irreversible-ceremony deferral. What is new is narrow: the counter's attach point (Read AC of F1D1/F1D2 rather than Execute of F1D0), an exhaustion UX, SEC-driven timeout sizing and wedge classification, and a status readout.
already-have.corrections:
1. Not novel as a whole. Part (a) duplicates #485 and part (b) duplicates #275; the proposal cites neither. Treat SE-08 as a refinement to fold into those two issues, not a new item.

2. Attach point differs from #485. #485 proposes E122 as a lifetime execute counter on the main F1D0 auth path (the Trezor shape). SE-08 puts LUC(E122) on the Read AC of F1D1/F1D2. Only push_ac_luc on META_EXECUTE exists and is silicon-validated (secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:1150, :1379). A Read-AC 'Auto(F1D0) && LUC(E122)' expression is unvalidated on this chip. That makes the cost M rather than S, since it needs a sacrificial-silicon receipt and S-3 profile work.

3. 'pq1 has only E120 (resettable) and E121 (duress)' is incomplete. E121 already climbs about once per unlock and is not resettable by a real-PIN unlock (limit 0x00FF_FFFF; secure/src/optiga/mod.rs:1370-1385). #485 calls this 'a partial analog, duress path only'. It gates F1D8, not the half_O read, so the gap is real but narrower than stated.

4. The proposal's own duress risk note is material. A read-path E122 bump on a real unlock with no mirrored bump on the duress read would break the validated timing twin (apdu.rs:238-246).

5. Part (b) exceeds the recorded se-3 scope. se-3 is 'strictly advisory (log + NV3007)... Do NOT wire into tamp-wipe' (docs/architecture/trezor-comparison-critical-port-2026-06.md:104; #275). Sizing PRL timeouts from SEC and reclassifying wedges as 'inconclusive-throttled' changes control flow on the page-124 burn path. It is compatible in spirit, because it reduces false wipes, but it is new behaviour that belongs under #119 (OP17-4) and needs its own review.

6. #485's fold target is stale. It says to land 'inside the #443 first-boot ceremony work', but #443 is CLOSED. #485 needs a new home, which is the S-3 / optiga-hw-counter provisioning profile.

7. Kind should be mixed: firmware plus an irreversible provisioning ceremony (Change=Never). It is gated by the deliberate S-1/S-2/S-3 deferral, so it cannot land standalone before the frozen S-3 profile.

8. The sizing example (200,000) is a product decision. Trezor uses 600,000 and the chip's E122 default is 600,000 (docs/secure-elements/OPTIGATRUSTM/commands-and-oids.md:359).

9. The repo_evidence lines are all substantially true today. Minor nit: reset_hw_pin_counter is at mod.rs:1620-1627 and reset_e120_via_transient_auth starts around :1672. The 'F1D1/F1D2 Read = Auto(F1D0) only, no LUC arm' fact is confirmed at apdu.rs:1182-1200 (with an optional Conf AND), consumed at mod.rs:1290 and :1330.

10. The OPTIGA SRM '>127 → up to 5 s' throttling figure and the Trezor line citations were not checked in this pass.

feasible.reason:
Part (a) as specified does not defend against its stated threat. The threat is an unbounded PIN-guessing oracle after a counter-reset bug. A guess is consumed at the Execute of the F1D0 AuthRef (the HMAC verify), and the half_O / master reads happen only after that verify has succeeded (secure/src/optiga/mod.rs:2582-2626: `hmac_verify OK` then step 7 reads). A LUC in the Read AC of F1D1/F1D2 is therefore decremented only by successful unlocks; every wrong guess costs zero E122 units. With E120 reset by a bug, the attacker still guesses without bound and needs exactly one budget unit for the final successful read.

The Trezor precedent is misapplied. Trezor places LUC(PIN_TOTAL_CTR) on the Execute AC of the stretching keys E200 (PIN_CMAC) and E0F3 (PIN_ECDH) (optiga.c:504-522, docs/core/misc/optiga.md rows E0F3/E200), which run on every attempt before the verify, right or wrong. pq1 has no chip-side stretching object on the guess path, so there is nowhere to hang the lifetime counter without a redesign.

Other problems with (a):
- Two units per unlock, not one: F1D1 and F1D2 are both read on each unlock (mod.rs:2617-2626), so the 200,000 sizing is off by 2x. The 120 s idle re-unlock also consumes budget.
- LUC inside a Read AC combined with `Auto AND Conf AND Luc` is unvalidated on silicon. The repo only ever emits LUC in an Execute AC (apdu.rs:1146-1157, `push_ac_luc` is used for F1D0/F1D8 Execute), and I did not find an SRM statement in the repo that LUC is honoured for Read. This is a guess until tested on sacrificial silicon.
- Change=Never is only irreversible once the object's LcsO is Operational. Trezor does this under `#if PRODUCTION` (optiga.c:333-340). On pq1 that is the unclosed S-1/S-3 lifecycle ceremony, so the proposal depends on a ship-blocker and is not a standalone S firmware change.

Part (b), the SEC (E0C5) read and throttle classification, and part (c), the read-only status, are sound, firmware-only, and need no board change. No pq1 hardware change is needed for any part.
feasible.corrections:
1. Move the lifetime counter onto the guess path. Two candidate designs:
   - Execute AC of F1D0 as `Luc(E120) AND Luc(E122)`. Two LUCs in one expression is unvalidated on Trezor and on pq1 and needs a silicon test.
   - The Trezor shape: add a chip-side stretching key (E200 AES-CMAC, Execute=Luc(E122)) whose output feeds the F1D0 HMAC input. This changes PIN derivation and forces re-provisioning of every bench board.
2. Mirror the change on the duress twin. F1D8 is executed on every unlock (mod.rs:1376-1380), so it needs the same extra APDU or AC (E123, or the same E122) or the duress path becomes timing-distinguishable.
3. Drop the Read-AC LUC on F1D1/F1D2, or keep it only as a secondary cap on post-auth reads. If kept, size it for two reads per unlock plus idle re-unlocks.
4. Irreversibility needs LcsO=Operational on E122, so this belongs in the S-1/S-3 frozen profile and ceremony. Kind is mixed (firmware + process), not firmware.
5. Cost is M, not S: redesign of the guess path, duress parity, sacrificial-silicon validation and bench re-provisioning. Part (b)/(c) alone is S and can be split out as its own P2 item.
6. Part (b) caveat: SEC decays only while the OPTIGA is powered, and pq1 gates the SE rail on PA8 with no battery or RTC. Trezor's "keep powered until SEC decays" (optiga_init.c:101-117, under USE_RTC) is not portable. The value on pq1 is classification and timeout sizing only, and the SEC read must not be able to defer the wipe.
7. The Trezor citations are otherwise accurate: E121 PIN_TOTAL_CTR, limit 600,000, Change=Never (optiga.c:52-54, 77, 482-502); SEC model at optiga_commands.c:80-110; OPTIGA_OID_SEC = 0xE0C5. The proposal omits that Trezor's E122 is PIN_HMAC_CTR and that Trezor binds the total counter via Execute, never Read.
